newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik gvt says will meet hostage-takers' demands.
newsitem.headline: Tajik gvt says will meet hostage-takers' demands.

text.p: The Tajik government said on Tuesday it would meet the demands of a rebel group holding several foreign aid workers hostage by allowing the return of other group members from Afghanistan to the ex-Soviet republic.

"At an urgent meeting held by (Tajik President Imomali) Rakhmonov in Dushanbe, the government has agreed to implement the fighters' demands," Rakhmonov's spokesman, Zafar Saidov, told Reuters by telephone.
However, Saidov said the method of exchange and whether the 40 group members would be allowed to return from their base in northern Afghanistan with their weapons had still to be decided.

Tajik rebel leader Rizvon Sadirov returned home from Afghanistan on Monday to help negotiate the release of hostages held by his brother Bakhrom, but appeared to offer little assistance once he arrived.

The rebels seized four United Nations military observers last Tuesday and later captured a carload of Russian reporters and four workers with the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR. Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukharov, who flew in to negotiate with the hostage-takers, was seized early on Saturday.

Two Red Cross workers also captured were released last week but hopes that the remaining captives would be released have been dashed repeatedly and the rebels have ignored appeals from international organisations.
